text: Some time later, during the rule of Artaxerxes king of Persia, there was a man named Ezra, son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest —

this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe well trained in the Law of Moses that the LORD, the God of Israel, had given, and because the LORD's hand was on him, the king granted him everything he requested.
Some of the Israelites, along with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, went up to Jerusalem too, in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of that seventh year of the king.
He had left Babylon on the first day of the first month and reached Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, since the good hand of his God was with him.
For Ezra had committed himself to studying the Law of the LORD, living it out, and teaching its statutes and rulings in Israel.
Here is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe, learned in the LORD's commands and the statutes given to Israel:
Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven. Greetings, and so on.
I now order that anyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel, including priests and Levites, who wishes to go with you to Jerusalem may go.
You are sent by the king and his seven advisers to inspect the condition of Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which is in your possession,
and to carry the silver and gold that the king and his advisers have freely given to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
together with all the silver and gold you obtain anywhere in the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings the people and priests give for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
With this money you are to buy, without delay, bulls, rams, and lambs, along with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and present them on the altar of your God's house in Jerusalem.
Whatever seems best to you and your fellow leaders to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do it in keeping with the will of your God.
Deliver before the God of Jerusalem all the articles entrusted to you for the service of the house of your God.
And whatever else is needed for the house of your God that falls to you to supply, you may draw from the royal treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, now command every treasurer of the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, requests of you, provide it promptly,
up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred measures of wheat, a hundred measures of wine, a hundred measures of oil, and salt without limit.
Whatever the God of heaven commands, let it be done fully for the house of the God of heaven, so that wrath does not fall on the realm of the king and his sons.
You are further informed that no tribute, tax, or toll may be charged against any priest, Levite, singer, gatekeeper, temple servant, or other worker of this house of God.

And you, Ezra, in keeping with the wisdom of your God that you carry, appoint magistrates and judges to govern all the people of the province Beyond the River who know the laws of your God — and teach those who do not know them.
Whoever does not obey the law of your God and the law of the king is to face strict judgment — death, exile, confiscation of property, or imprisonment.
Praise the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who put it into the king's heart to bring honor to the LORD's house in Jerusalem in this way,

and who showed me such kindness before the king, his advisers, and all his powerful officials. I was strengthened, because the hand of the LORD my God was on me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
